card.name: Great-power geopolitics text, linking words
card.fires_on: Small linking words, verbs and punctuation in English essays about international relations (US, China, Asia, world order), just before a country, region or global-order term would come next.

modes.label: Linking words before nations
modes.description: Words like the, with, by, to or in right before a group of states or a region.
modes.example: emerging powers have largely supported<< the>> U.S. armada to ensure that

modes.label: Verbs and modifiers in power politics
modes.description: Verbs or hyphenated modifiers about alliances and regional order.
modes.example: China is chafing at the current US<<-led>> regional order of sovereign states, in which

modes.label: Stray spots in the same text
modes.description: Digits or commas inside the same kind of foreign-policy essay.
modes.example: about 5,0<<0>>0 died. But it wasn’t until

card.writes: It pushes toward Chinese words for member states, world economy, Asia-Pacific and great powers, and away from words for nationwide or domestic.
card.plain: It marks places in world-politics writing where a word about nations, regions or the global order is likely to come next.

China is chafing at the current US<<-led>> regional order of sovereign states, in which
